note: Required first name for pension fund registration is backed by F-SC-002 and F-SC-015.
F-SC-003 and the 'Last name is required.' error in F-SC-015 back it.
Required field and the DD.MM.YYYY format are backed by F-SC-004, F-SC-005 and F-SC-015.
HR's full address need, completeness reason and envelope-style form are backed by F-TR-009 and F-TR-010.
House number is named as part of the full address by HR, and the notes correctly flag the open question.
Postcode is named as part of the complete address that HR needs.
HR needs the full address including town, as on an envelope, so it is always asked and required.
The country is part of the full address (F-TR-009/010), and F-TR-034/036/037/040 back its use as country of residence for source tax.
Nationality is needed for the source tax decision for residents (F-TR-038/037), and F-TR-034 plus G-01 support not asking people who live abroad; the expression matches the wording.
The permit type is needed for non-Swiss residents because C permit holders are treated like Swiss nationals (F-TR-025/037/039), and the asked-when condition matches its expression.

The restriction to asking only residents of Switzerland is not backed: the fund marks Canton required for everyone, and F-SC-017 says what applies to people living abroad (and residence versus work canton) is unclear.
F-TR-014/015/018/019, F-SC-008 and G-08 back an always-asked, always-required first working day that HR confirms and the insurance start date is derived from.
Options, always-asked/required and the three needs are backed by F-SC-010/011/015, F-TR-029 and F-TR-030.
Format, married-only display and required-when-shown are backed by F-TR-021 and F-SC-012 to F-SC-016.
F-TR-031 and F-TR-032 back the need and the condition, and the expression matches the text.
F-TR-032 says the permit is only needed if the spouse is not Swiss, and 'if they have one' backs the optional answer.
F-TR-031 and F-TR-032 back the need, and G-01 backs asking only when the answer can change the outcome.
The statement, every table row and the expression match F-TR-034, F-TR-006, F-TR-025, F-TR-030, F-TR-037 and F-TR-005.

The cited facts never mention a pension fund canton question or say it is skipped for residents abroad and asked for residents in Switzerland (AC-02.2.2, AC-02.2.3), and the claim that source tax and HR receive the country of residence is not backed either.

The cited facts leave open whether the canton means residence or work and what applies to people abroad (F-SC-006, F-SC-017), so asking only Swiss-resident employees and naming the item residence_canton is an unbacked assumption.

AC-04.4.5 states that HR has checked the rules against Stefan, Maria and Tomás and that gaps go through OQ-05, but the facts only show HR hedging ('I think that's it') and say nothing about such a check or that handling; the other criteria are backed by F-TR-005/025/030/034/037/040.
